title: opum-quest mod: remove fleet mode; no auto-start in teammate, headless or workflow processes; guarded, bounded clocks
description:
Filed from DEC-172 (4bg) item 1, read from opum-doc origin/dev at ce3374b (opum-ai/opum-doc#896). (4bg) is item 1 of that decision's spec for this repository: quest-cli (opum-quest), HIGH, and it blocks re-enabling the board plugin.

Operator's first-party ruling, verbatim from (4bg): "remove fleet mode from the add-on. make sure there is no other bug. proceed with the other recommendations -> teammates, and dynamic workflows should not be running the mode automatically. also make sure that heads up so you know mod is disabled too".

The five acceptance criteria below are (4bg) item 1 (a)-(e), verbatim.

The incident this answers (recorded in (4bf) and (4bg); relay OA-2026-10-12-01, seq 617): load average reached 315/320/306 at 02:54:55Z with 155 to 212 live `quest task list` processes, all direct children of Claude processes, and the three active jobs were stalled. opum-quest 0.13.0's board auto-opened in EVERY Claude process (session.start calls openPane), refreshing every 60s over all 13 repositories; refresh()'s isRefreshing guard bounded only that path, and the unguarded checkAlerts (~120s) and countUncommitted stacked on top, giving the breadth (every process x 13 repos x 1/min). The operator disabled the plugin at user scope ((4bf)); re-enabling it requires this fix released AND an operator yes.

The audit findings this task closes, named in (4bg), all in the installed opum-quest 0.13.0 (byte-identical to origin/dev):
- quest A1: the checkAlerts clock (register.tsx:635-644) has no in-flight guard, and runs 2 spawns x every repo with an unbounded Promise.all.
- quest A2: the refresh clock is registered inside session.start with no once-guard, so it re-registers on every resume; its `void (async...)` wrapper defeats the clock's serialization, and countUncommitted is unguarded.
- quest A3: readScopes uses an unbounded Promise.all.
- quest A4: there is no session.end handler, so no timer is ever cancelled.

Assignee opum-control per DEC-152 OQ-1 ((4bg)/(4i): new dispatch tasks are created with the assignee from the start).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Remove fleet mode completely. The board, alerts and the dashboard tool read only the session's own repository. Remove: the root and repos options and discovery (resolveFleet, discoverRoot, reposUnder, discoveryNote); the Scope type and its toggle; the repo Select; the grouped-by-repo list and the "in the fleet" headers; the dashboard tool's scope parameter. A stored "fleet" scope from an older version reads as local, with no error.

Auto-start gate: on session.start, when !e.isInteractive OR $.env.get("CLAUDECODE") === "1", open no pane and register no clock. An explicit open by the person (command or tool) still works and polls only while shown.

Every clock is registered once per process (module guard), its handle is kept, and it is cancelled at session.end. The WHOLE callback is guarded in flight: a tick that finds the previous one running is skipped. That covers refresh, countUncommitted and checkAlerts.
Every subprocess keeps a timeout, and no tick spawns more than 3 processes.

Proof, run both ways: a process marked CLAUDECODE=1, and one with isInteractive false, each spawn 0 quest/git children over 5 minutes; an interactive process stays within the bound; a soak of 8 interactive processes over 10 minutes shows no growth in child-process count, with the counts reported; `claude plugin validate` lists the CLAUDECODE env read.

finalSummary:
DEC-172 (4bg) item 1, all five parts, in hooks/register.tsx and the surfaces around it.

(a) Fleet mode removed. The board, the alerts and the dashboard tool read this session's own repository and nothing else: resolveFleet, discoverRoot, reposUnder, discoveryNote, the root/repos plugin options, the Scope type and its toggle, the repo Select, the grouped-by-repo list and the "in the fleet" wording are gone, with the tool's scope parameter and filterRows' repo argument. A stored view from a version that had fleet mode carries scope and is ACCEPTED -- it reads as local rather than being refused.

(b) Auto-start gate. session.start registers the dashboard tool and then stops when !e.isInteractive or $.env.get("CLAUDECODE") === "1": no pane, no clock, no read-back -- so a teammate, headless or workflow process spawns no child for a view nobody draws. A person's explicit open still works in a gated process and starts the clock from then on.

(c) Clocks. Both are once per process behind a module guard, their handles kept, cancelled at session.end, and the WHOLE tick callback is guarded in flight so a tick that finds the previous one running is SKIPPED. A person's EXPLICIT refresh is COALESCED rather than dropped: one more read runs after the current one.

(d) No tick spawns more than three subprocesses, and every subprocess already carried a timeout. A refresh tick runs two; an alerts tick runs its two reads plus, inside the same budget, the one task view that tells a Done task from a Closed one -- carrying the rest of its departures into the next tick rather than dropping them. One real defect was found building this: resolveLocal re-ran its git child on every call, so a refresh tick spawned FOUR; it now resolves once per root.

(e) AC5 proof, REAL processes -- a real claude with --plugin-dir at a staged copy of this branch, PATH shims logging every mod child, and the installed opum-quest plugin disabled per run via a scratch config's enabledPlugins (so only this branch's build could be running). Counts, with the gate removed as the control in each case:

- teammate, CLAUDECODE=1, 300s: 0 mod children (1229 ps samples, max concurrent 0).
- headless (-p over a held-open stream-json pipe), 300s: 0 mod children (1230 samples, max 0), against its OWN gate-removed control on the same rig, 180s: 10 mod children.
- interactive person, 180s: 11 mod children, max concurrent 2 -- inside the bound of 3.
- control, teammate with the gate removed, 120s: 9 mod children.
- SOAK, 8 interactive processes, 600s each: 28 mod children each (17 quest + 11 git .quest reads), IDENTICAL across all eight -- no growth; 0 leftovers after the kills.
- Load during the soak: 3.94 before, 3.43 peak sampled, 2.20 after -- never near the (4bf) ceiling of 15.
- `claude plugin validate` lists: env reads: CLAUDECODE.

DISCARDED RUN, recorded so the trail is honest: the first headless attempt used `tail -f /dev/null | claude -p`, which errors with "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument" -- so BOTH its rows read 0 and neither is evidence of anything. Its own gate-removed control is what caught it; the rows above are the re-run on the stream-json rig.

Gates: bun run check exit 0 on the head (CLI suite, mod suite 43 pass / 0 fail, lore check, typecheck, lint); `claude plugin validate` passed. The shipped reference (docs/reference/quest-board-hooks-module-in-the-opum-quest-plugin.md) carries the refresh semantics verbatim as ruled, and the generated plugin skill, plugin manifest and the mod's test suite are updated in the same change.

AC5 RE-RUN ON THE FIXED HEAD, with the PER-TICK measurement the round-1 blocker showed was missing.

Round 1 (review-assignment attempt 1 at 19106caa) found a BLOCKER: checkAlerts seeded its child budget with read.length -- the number of repositories read, always 1 -- while readAlerts spawns TWO children per repository (a decision list and a task list). An alerts tick therefore permitted two task view look-ups on top of its two reads: FOUR subprocesses against a budget of three. Fixed by seeding with read.length * 2.

WHY THE FIRST TABLE MISSED IT. That table measured ps max_concurrent (2), but (4bg)(d) bounds children PER TICK, and a tick's children finish one after another, so concurrency can never see four sequential children. The shim log's timestamps are now grouped into ticks PER CLOCK: the 60s refresh and the 120s alerts clocks coincide every other minute, so a time-only grouping would merge two ticks and overstate either.

PER-TICK CHILDREN, fixed build, interactive and soak runs: interactive person 180s -- alerts ticks [1,1,1] max 1, refresh ticks [3,2,2,2] max 3. Soak, each of the eight 600s processes, IDENTICAL -- alerts ticks [1,1,1,1,1,1,1] max 1, refresh ticks [3,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2] max 3. Every tick is at or under three.

POSITIVE CONTROL for that measurement, which is what makes the 3s mean something: the same measurement on a build with the OLD seed and a canned `quest` whose open set shrinks after 90s, so the second alerts tick needs look-ups. Alerts ticks [2,4,2,2] max 4 on the old seed against [2,3,3,2] max 3 on the fixed build -- with the SAME totals (20 mod children) and ps max_concurrent 1 on both. So the per-tick count sees the defect and the fix closes it.

AC5 RE-RUN, fixed build, stage rebuilt from the head, installed opum-quest disabled per run:
- teammate, CLAUDECODE=1, 300s: 0 mod children.
- headless (-p over a held-open stream-json pipe), 300s: 0 mod children, against its OWN gate-removed control on the same rig and a stated shorter window (60s), which spawned 5. A teammate control does not validate the headless rig, so this one is separate.
- interactive person, 180s: 11 mod children.
- control, teammate with the gate removed, 120s: 9 mod children.
- SOAK, 8 interactive processes, 600s each: 28 mod children each, IDENTICAL across all eight.
- Load during the soak: 2.21 before, 3.85 peak sampled, 1.50 after -- far below the (4bf) ceiling of 15. 0 leftovers after the kills.
- `claude plugin validate` lists: env reads: CLAUDECODE.

DISCARDED RUN, kept so the trail is honest: the first headless rig (tail -f /dev/null | claude -p) errored with "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument", so both its rows read 0 and neither is evidence of anything; its own gate-removed control caught it.

Also corrected with the blocker: the two kit tests that had pinned the over-budget behaviour (the batched-toast test now produces more than three changes WITHIN the budget, and the completion-toast test is driven across ticks, which pins one-look-up-per-tick).
